title: Surjectivity on global sections of an affine extension with quasi-coherent ends
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be its affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal F_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_3$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Then $\Gamma(X,g):\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_2)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_3)$ is surjective.

source.place: Schemes, Tag 01IE, lemma-extension-quasi-coherent, proof from Pick m to its end

proof.text: For m in Gamma(X,F_3), form the ideal I of a in R for which a*m is in the image of Gamma(X,F_2). To prove surjectivity it suffices to prove I=R. At every prime p, sheaf epimorphism gives a local lift s on a principal neighbourhood D(f), with f outside p.

For each point z of V(f), choose D(g) containing z with a second lift s-prime. The difference over D(fg) belongs to the kernel F_1. Since F_1 is associated to its global section module, clear a power of f from its localization over D(fg) to obtain a section over D(g). Adding this correction to f^n*s-prime extends f^n*s over D(f) union D(g), with image f^n*m.

Quasi-compactness of V(f) gives finitely many g_j and a common exponent n. On D(g_j*g_k), the differences between the corrected lifts are sections of F_1 whose localization at f is zero. The localization zero criterion gives a common additional power f^N killing all differences. Multiplication by it makes the lifts agree on every overlap; the sheaf axiom glues them over X, producing a global lift of f^(N+n)*m. Thus f^(N+n) is in I and is outside p.

The ideal I is contained in no prime ideal; a proper ideal is contained in a maximal ideal, so I=R. In particular 1*m lifts. This is surjectivity of the map of global section modules, equivalent to Epi in ModuleCat. This includes the zero ring, where the module category is trivial.
